Operation Victoria — Historical Reference Board

Period photographs of the working machinery of the 1889 port, and the specific modelling decision each one drove. All plates are from Ocean Steamships: A Popular Account of their Construction, Development, Management and Appliances (New York, 1891), a public-domain work contemporaneous with the ports being built. Every plate below is a photograph or engraving made in or before 1891 — nothing later than 1889 has been used to justify a design decision.

Port A - passenger harbour

Port B - industrial harbour

Sourcing discipline. These boards justify form and arrangement, not literal copying. Where a plate shows an American or Mediterranean arrangement the decision recorded beside it is the British-1889 adaptation actually modelled.

Exclusions. Belfast's Thompson Graving Dock (1911), the Arrol gantry (1905 onward) and Southampton's No. 5 dry dock (1896) are outside the 1889 horizon and are deliberately absent from both ports. See HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE.md.
